state.requirement: Make short links expire sooner. Ask for default lifetime, maximum lifetime and whether existing links are affected before implementation.
state.clarification:
1. Default lifetime is 30 days from creation when
   expiresAt is omitted.

2. Maximum lifetime is 90 days from creation.
   Reject requests exceeding this limit with HTTP 400.
   Reject expiration timestamps that are not in the future.

3. Existing links must remain unchanged.
   Apply the new policy only to newly created links.

4. Preserve existing API contracts and idempotency behavior.
   Avoid unnecessary database migrations.

5. Add focused tests for default expiration, explicit valid
   expiration, maximum boundary, invalid expiration,
   and backward compatibility.

6. Keep the implementation minimal and preserve all
   unrelated production behavior.

requirements.summary: Clarification resolves all three blocking decisions. Default lifetime: 30 days from creation when expiresAt is omitted on POST /api/v1/urls. Maximum lifetime: 90 days from creation; a request whose expiresAt exceeds creation time plus 90 days is rejected with HTTP 400 (no clamping). An expiresAt that is not in the future continues to be rejected (HTTP 400 Invalid expiration). Existing links remain unchanged: the new policy applies only to newly created links, so no backfill and no Flyway migration are needed (V1__links.sql is untouched and expires_at stays nullable, so legacy NULL rows keep never expiring). Existing API contracts (request/response shape, 201 body with code and shortPath, 409 on alias conflict, 503 on code exhaustion) and idempotency behavior are preserved. Redirect logic (GET /{code}) is unchanged. Assumptions for non-blocking details: the 'now' reference is a single Instant captured per request and used for both the default and the max boundary; a value exactly equal to now+90 days is accepted (the limit is inclusive); the 30-day and 90-day values may be held as constants or application.yml properties with those defaults, whichever is minimal, as no configurability was requested. Tests are added for default expiration, explicit valid expiration, maximum boundary, invalid expiration, and backward compatibility, while existing ShortenerTest tests keep passing.
acceptance: POST /api/v1/urls without expiresAt returns 201 and stores expires_at equal to creation time + 30 days (within a small test tolerance or via an injected clock).
POST /api/v1/urls with an explicit expiresAt in the future and at or before creation time + 90 days returns 201 and stores exactly the supplied expiresAt.
POST /api/v1/urls with expiresAt exactly at creation time + 90 days is accepted (boundary inclusive), tested with a controlled clock.
POST /api/v1/urls with expiresAt beyond creation time + 90 days (e.g. +90 days and 1 second) returns HTTP 400 and no row is inserted.
POST /api/v1/urls with expiresAt in the past or equal to now returns HTTP 400 with the 'Invalid expiration' message.

Existing links are unchanged: no new Flyway migration is added, V1__links.sql is not modified, and pre-existing rows (including those with NULL expires_at) retain their values; verified by test or by confirming no data-modifying SQL exists.
Redirect behavior is unchanged: GET /{code} returns 302 for active, non-expired links (and legacy NULL expires_at links), and 404 without incrementing clicks for expired or inactive links.

Existing API contracts are preserved: 201 response body keys code and shortPath, 409 on alias conflict, 400 on invalid URL/alias, 503 on code allocation exhaustion, and alias/code retry behavior are unchanged.
Existing ShortenerTest tests (acceptsHttps, rejectsUnsafeScheme, rejectsCredentials) still pass.
Changes are minimal and limited to expiration policy logic plus focused tests; no unrelated production behavior is modified.

plan.summary: Add an expiration policy to link creation in Shortener.java only. Capture one Instant 'now' per request. If expiresAt is omitted, set it to now + 30 days. If expiresAt is not after now, keep returning HTTP 400 'Invalid expiration'. If expiresAt is after now + 90 days (inclusive limit), return HTTP 400 with no insert. Otherwise store the supplied value. Redirect, analytics, alias/code retry, 409/503 handling, response body, and the DB schema stay unchanged. No Flyway migration is added, so existing rows, including legacy NULL expires_at, are untouched. To test boundaries deterministically, extract the policy into a small pure static helper (e.g. resolveExpiration(Instant requested, Instant now)) that unit tests can call with a fixed 'now'. Add focused tests for default, explicit valid, exact 90-day boundary, over-limit, past/equal-to-now, and backward compatibility, while the existing ShortenerTest tests keep passing.
tasks: 1. Re-read Shortener.create() and confirm the current flow: validate URL, validate alias, check expiresAt is in the future, then the insert loop that passes null when expiresAt is omitted.

2. In Shortener.java add constants DEFAULT_LIFETIME = Duration.ofDays(30) and MAX_LIFETIME = Duration.ofDays(90), and import java.time.Duration. Plain constants are the minimal choice because configurability was not requested, so application.yml is not touched.

3. Add a package-private static helper Instant resolveExpiration(Instant requested, Instant now) in Shortener.java. If requested is null, return now.plus(DEFAULT_LIFETIME). If requested is not after now, throw ResponseStatusException(400, 'Invalid expiration'). If requested is after now.plus(MAX_LIFETIME), throw ResponseStatusException(400, with a clear message such as 'Expiration exceeds maximum lifetime'). Otherwise return requested unchanged. The 90-day boundary is inclusive and there is no clamping.

4. Update create() to capture a single Instant now = Instant.now() per request, compute Instant expiresAt = resolveExpiration(input.expiresAt(), now) before the insert loop, and replace the null-handling in the insert with Timestamp.from(expiresAt). Keep validation order (URL, alias, expiration), the retry loop, the 409/503 handling, and the 201 body {code, shortPath} exactly as they are. Because resolution happens before the loop, an over-limit request inserts no row.

5. Verify there is no data impact: do not add a migration, leave V1__links.sql unmodified, and leave expires_at nullable so legacy NULL rows keep never expiring. Leave the redirect query (expires_at is null or expires_at>now()) and the analytics endpoint untouched.

6. Add focused unit tests to src/test/java/demo/ShortenerTest.java (or a new ExpirationPolicyTest in the same package) using a fixed 'now'. Cover: default (null gives now+30d), explicit valid (now+10d returned unchanged), maximum boundary (exactly now+90d accepted), over limit (now+90d+1s throws ResponseStatusException with 400), invalid (past and equal-to-now throw 400), and backward compatibility (existing tests unchanged, and the helper does not alter a valid explicit value).

7. Optionally add a lightweight check that creation with an over-limit expiresAt throws 400 before touching the DB, for example by calling create() with a mocked JdbcTemplate and verifying no update() call. Use Mockito from spring-boot-starter-test and avoid needing a live Postgres or Redis. Also verify the success path passes now+30d to db.update when expiresAt is omitted, with a tolerance.

8. Run the full test suite (mvn test) and confirm that acceptsHttps, rejectsUnsafeScheme, rejectsCredentials, and the new tests all pass. Review the diff to confirm that only expiration policy code and tests changed and that no unrelated production behavior was modified.

design.summary: Design contract for 30-day default / 90-day max link expiration, applied to new links only. Scope: one production file (Shortener.java) and one new test file. No API shape change, no DB or Flyway change, no application.yml change. Agent A owns production code and Agent B owns tests. They share only the contract below. API: POST /api/v1/urls keeps the same request {url, alias?, expiresAt?} and the same 201 body {code, shortPath}. Validation order stays URL, alias, expiration. Expiration rules: omitted expiresAt becomes now+30d; expiresAt <= now returns 400 'Invalid expiration'; expiresAt > now+90d returns 400 'Expiration exceeds maximum lifetime' (no clamping, limit inclusive, no row inserted); otherwise the supplied value is stored unchanged. 'now' is one Instant captured per request. 409 alias conflict, 503 code exhaustion, the 5-attempt retry loop, redirect GET /{code} and analytics stay unchanged. Persistence: expires_at stays nullable, V1__links.sql is untouched, no new migration and no backfill, so legacy rows (including NULL expires_at) are unchanged. Security and failure handling: expiration is validated server-side before any DB call, and every rejection is a ResponseStatusException 400 with a fixed message that does not echo input. No secrets or new config. Shared contract signature in package demo: `static Instant resolveExpiration(Instant requested, Instant now)` in class Shortener (package-private, pure, no I/O), plus constants `static final Duration DEFAULT_LIFETIME = Duration.ofDays(30)` and `static final Duration MAX_LIFETIME = Duration.ofDays(90)`.
tasks: AGENT A (production) - edit src/main/java/demo/Shortener.java only. Add import java.time.Duration. Add package-private constants DEFAULT_LIFETIME=Duration.ofDays(30) and MAX_LIFETIME=Duration.ofDays(90).

AGENT A - add `static Instant resolveExpiration(Instant requested, Instant now)`: if requested==null return now.plus(DEFAULT_LIFETIME); if !requested.isAfter(now) throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST,"Invalid expiration"); if requested.isAfter(now.plus(MAX_LIFETIME)) throw new ResponseStatusException(HttpStatus.BAD_REQUEST,"Expiration exceeds maximum lifetime"); else return requested unchanged. The boundary now+90d exactly is accepted.

AGENT A - in create(): keep validate(input.url()) and the alias check first. Then `Instant expiresAt = resolveExpiration(input.expiresAt(), Instant.now());` replaces the old inline expiration check and runs before the retry loop, so a rejected request never reaches db.update. The insert passes Timestamp.from(expiresAt) as the third bind argument (no null branch). Leave the retry loop, DuplicateKeyException to 409, the 503 fallthrough, the 201 body, redirect(), analytics(), validate(), the Create record and the constructor exactly as they are.
AGENT A - do not touch pom.xml, application.yml, or anything under src/main/resources/db/migration. Do not add a migration or any data-modifying SQL. Make no other behavior changes.

AGENT B (tests) - create the new file src/test/java/demo/ExpirationPolicyTest.java in package demo. Do not edit ShortenerTest.java, so the three existing tests (acceptsHttps, rejectsUnsafeScheme, rejectsCredentials) stay untouched and cannot conflict with Agent A. Use JUnit 5 and, for the create() tests, Mockito from spring-boot-starter-test; no Spring context, Postgres or Redis.

AGENT B - pure helper tests with fixed NOW=Instant.parse("2030-01-01T00:00:00Z"), calling Shortener.resolveExpiration(requested, NOW): (1) default: null returns NOW.plus(30 days); (2) explicit valid: NOW.plus(10 days) is returned unchanged; (3) maximum boundary: exactly NOW.plus(90 days) is accepted and returned unchanged; (4) over limit: NOW.plus(90 days).plusSeconds(1) throws ResponseStatusException with getStatusCode().value()==400; (5) invalid: NOW.minusSeconds(1) and NOW itself each throw ResponseStatusException with status 400 and reason "Invalid expiration".

AGENT B - create() tests with mock(JdbcTemplate.class) and mock(StringRedisTemplate.class), new Shortener(db, redis) and new Shortener.Create("https://example.com/a", null, expiresAt). (a) Omitted expiresAt: record Instant before/after around the call; assert status 201, body keys code and shortPath, and capture the Timestamp bind argument of db.update(anyString(), any(), any(), captor.capture()); assert it lies within [before+30d, after+30d]. (b) Explicit now+10d: the captured Timestamp equals Timestamp.from(supplied). (c) Over-limit now+91d: assertThrows ResponseStatusException with status 400 and verifyNoInteractions(db). (d) Past expiresAt: status 400 and verifyNoInteractions(db).

AGENT B - backward compatibility tests: assert that the helper never alters a valid explicit value, and that a mocked db.update throwing DuplicateKeyException with an alias set still yields ResponseStatusException 409. Do not assert on migration files. Keep the tests deterministic, with no sleeps and no real clock comparisons beyond the tolerance window above.

Cross-agent rules: both agents only generate files and run no commands. The helper name, signature, constants and the two exact messages ('Invalid expiration', 'Expiration exceeds maximum lifetime') are the only coupling. Both agents must keep the changes minimal and leave all unrelated production behavior intact.
